Hi PV'ers!

I started ProtectVoat on August 15 with this post. This was before 'she' took over AskVoat, before Atko announced Voat was moving to the US, before hecho, before /v/news had a cupcake incident. I know, it feels like ages ago in Voat time, huh?

How did we start?

My thoughts behind PV were summed up in the first comment:

Haha :-)

Voat has a unique value proposition in the internet media landscape. That VP attracts hostile people who'd rather we stay on Reddit where they can censor us and advertise to us.

This sub is for documenting those attempts.

What a start we have had. We've worked with several subs to stop their censorship, we were invited on the transition council of AskVoat, we've had heated discussions with mods who thought they were the owners of their communities - when in fact, communities should belong to the communities themselves.

The true spirit of PV ...

We quickly created our Protect Voat Charter. Find it here if you need a brush-up. PV'ers believe in a free Voat. In a place where we can all exist as long as we allow others the same right. In a place where we tolerate racists and angry feminists alike, because we know free speech has to be broadly applied for a true community to arise.

The only people who can't feel at home on Voat are those that won't allow other people the freedoms they themselves take for granted.

... has to include ourselves

In the past weeks, the PV mod group has had some very healthy discussions around moderation of PV itself. A divide in our group surfaced, we've examined it amicably and I took the decision that PV'ers deserve the mod team that offers them the most free speech.

Specifically, to avoid speculation, we stumbled across our Charter's §3.2:

3.2 We believe this subverse should be for documentation of censorship, shilling or unwelcome advertising. Other topics are welcome elsewhere.

This paragraph has been debated before, but the interpretation of it has been harder from my and Needlestack's side than from other mods'. And that divide can't exist if we're true to what we preach.

So ... that's it

We preach that we must always err on the side of free speech if in doubt. And that goes for ourselves, too:

To allow for PV to run smoothly, I'm therefore resigning from PV. I'm handing over to the next-most senior mod, Kevdude, from the moment of posting this (practically, L1 transitions take some time due to admin backlog). In reality, however, this has always been the users' sub - not mine nor any other mod's. And I can guarantee it'll stay that way under Kevdude and Crensch. So keep moderating this place yourselves, PVers!

With me leaves Needlestack. She's an amazing person, but she agrees with me on §3.2 and neither of us want to stay in the way of a true free speech PV.

Shut uuuuuuuup!!!

I know, right? You can look forward to less of my long, boring mod posts now! And since mods are really just janitors, please focus your energy elsewhere.

I'll see you around, assholes :-)
